title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL Powers Specialized Agents with Multimodal Reasoning | NVIDIA Technical Blog
gist: NVIDIA launches Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, an open 120B MoE (12B active) multimodal agent model distilled from Nemotron 3 Ultra, with vendor-claimed throughput gains, customer post-training cost cuts, and a stack of NVFP4, speculative decoding and Dynamo optimizations tied to its hardware.

themes.theme: Model design and agent use cases

insights.claim: NVIDIA's Nemotron 3.5 Super VL is an open, customizable multimodal model with 120B total parameters in a mixture-of-experts design that activates 12B per token, aimed at enterprise agentic workflows.
insights.speaker: Chris Alexiuk
insights.so_what: Shows NVIDIA pushing open mid-size MoE models that keep inference cost low and run on its own hardware.
insights.locator: Opening paragraphs

insights.claim: Nemotron 3.5 Super VL merges reasoning, tool use and text/image/document/video understanding into one model so teams need not deploy separate text and vision-language models or pass context between them.
insights.speaker: Chris Alexiuk
insights.so_what: Model consolidation lowers deployment complexity and serving footprint for agent builders.
insights.locator: The model combines reasoning, instruction following, and tool use

insights.claim: NVIDIA positions the model within a tiered system: Nemotron 3.5 Lightning for high-volume text tasks, Nemotron 3.5 Super VL for specialized multistep multimodal work, and Nemotron 3 Ultra for complex planning and orchestration.
insights.speaker: Chris Alexiuk
insights.so_what: Signals a multi-model routing architecture for enterprise agents, which drives mixed-size inference demand.
insights.locator: Why Nemotron 3.5 Super VL for specialized agents?

insights.claim: Target agent workloads are coding, web research, document intelligence, cybersecurity triage and video understanding.
insights.speaker: Chris Alexiuk
insights.so_what: Indicates which enterprise verticals NVIDIA expects to monetize with agent inference.
insights.locator: Why Nemotron 3.5 Super VL for specialized agents?

insights.claim: Organizations are post-training Nemotron 3.5 Super VL to outperform frontier models on accuracy and efficiency in specific production workflows across cybersecurity, finance and healthcare.
insights.speaker: Chris Alexiuk
insights.so_what: Supports the view that specialized small/mid models erode frontier-model pricing power on narrow tasks.
insights.locator: Customize Nemotron 3.5 Super VL for domain data, tools, and policies

insights.claim: Scale AI post-trained the model for automated vendor credit processing at Skydance Corporation, with inference cost expected to fall 40x and latency 5x.
insights.speaker: Chris Alexiuk
insights.so_what: A concrete cost-reduction datapoint, though a projection ('will decrease') from a vendor blog.
insights.locator: Scale AI, an AI data and technology provider

insights.claim: Ramp is converting receipt images to structured JSON with the model and expects up to 50% higher throughput and 10x lower latency.
insights.speaker: Chris Alexiuk
insights.so_what: Fintech back-office automation is an early production use case for multimodal open models.
insights.locator: Ramp, a financial operations platform provider

insights.claim: AI21 and Alice post-trained the model for threat intelligence and vulnerability analysis and improved accuracy by 41%.
insights.speaker: Chris Alexiuk
insights.so_what: Security is a showcased vertical for tuned open models.
insights.locator: AI21 and Alice post-trained

insights.claim: NVIDIA is releasing open datasets alongside the model, including agentic tool-use, finance reasoning, instruction-following, long-context and 40 vision-language datasets, and offers NeMo tools (AutoModel, Data Designer, RL, Gym) for SFT, LoRA and RL.
insights.speaker: Chris Alexiuk
insights.so_what: NVIDIA is bundling data, recipes and tooling to pull customization workloads into its software stack.
insights.locator: Alongside Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, NVIDIA is releasing open datasets

insights.claim: On CharXiv chart reasoning, Nemotron 3.5 Super VL scored 80.8% versus 63% for Nemotron 3 Nano Omni, reaching 84% with Python code interpretation, helped by diverse data generated with NeMo Data Designer.
insights.speaker: Chris Alexiuk
insights.so_what: Synthetic data generation is cited as the driver of multimodal gains.
insights.locator: Diverse training data generated with NeMo Data Designer

insights.claim: On Hermes Bench the model scores 63.44% versus 56.33% for Nemotron 3 Ultra, and on LangChain evals 87.05% versus 84.3%, so the smaller distilled model beats its larger teacher on agent tasks.
insights.speaker: Chris Alexiuk
insights.so_what: Distilled mid-size models can surpass larger parents on agentic evals, a deflationary signal for inference compute per task.
insights.locator: Table 1

insights.claim: NVIDIA claims up to 5x higher single-GPU throughput for agentic tasks versus similarly sized open models and 4x faster task completion, with an independent EXO Labs evaluation placing it on the accuracy/completion-time Pareto frontier on DGX Spark.
insights.speaker: Chris Alexiuk
insights.so_what: Efficiency claims are vendor-sourced; watch independent replication.
insights.locator: Accuracy and efficiency across agent tasks

insights.claim: The model was distilled from Nemotron 3 Ultra using the SkewReverse loss and multi-teacher on-policy distillation, with Perplexity datasets aiding mid-training and Prime Intellect environments aiding teacher models.
insights.speaker: Chris Alexiuk
insights.so_what: Shows an ecosystem (Nemotron Coalition) contributing data and environments to NVIDIA's open models.
insights.locator: Building a strong base model

insights.claim: NVIDIA added 10B Indic tokens in continued pretraining and is releasing a roughly 2.8T-token dataset across 22 Indian languages built with IIT Madras and AI4Bharat.
insights.speaker: Chris Alexiuk
insights.so_what: Indic-language data is a strategic play for sovereign and regional AI demand in India.
insights.locator: Continued pretraining with high-quality natural and synthetic data

insights.claim: LiLiCorr, an open speculative decoding technique, evaluates token candidates jointly across a draft and delivers up to 2.3x faster token generation than no speculation on DGX Spark.
insights.speaker: Chris Alexiuk
insights.so_what: Algorithmic decoding gains cut cost per token without new silicon.
insights.locator: LiLiCorr: An open speculative decoding technique

insights.claim: The NVFP4 recipe uses 4-bit weights and activations on Blackwell, with quantization-aware distillation matching the original BF16 outputs, adding no inference overhead and enabling an NVFP4 KV cache instead of FP8.
insights.speaker: Chris Alexiuk
insights.so_what: Low-precision formats tie model efficiency to Blackwell hardware and strengthen NVIDIA's platform lock-in.
insights.locator: NVFP4 and mixed precision

insights.claim: Multi-token prediction gives the model an internal drafter that proposes several tokens verified in one forward pass, reducing compute-intensive verification steps.
insights.speaker: Chris Alexiuk
insights.so_what: MTP is becoming a standard feature for lowering agent latency.
insights.locator: Multi-token prediction

insights.claim: Agent workloads repeatedly resend system prompts, tool definitions and history, so prefix caching that preserves attention caches and Mamba recurrent states is central to efficiency; the architecture is hybrid with Mamba layers.
insights.speaker: Chris Alexiuk
insights.so_what: KV-cache capacity and management is a key bottleneck for agentic serving, favoring memory-rich systems.
insights.locator: Context reuse across agent turns

insights.claim: With NVIDIA Dynamo on 16 B200 GPUs at 50 tokens/sec/user, KV-aware routing with session affinity and KV cache offload serves up to 8x as many users and cuts first-token latency by 85%.
insights.speaker: Chris Alexiuk
insights.so_what: Software-level serving gains raise effective capacity of installed GPUs.
insights.locator: Simplify production deployment with NVIDIA NIM and NVIDIA Dynamo

insights.claim: The release ships base, post-trained and NVFP4 checkpoints with recipes, data and RL environments, and a very broad partner list spans hosted inference providers (CoreWeave, Together AI, Nebius, Lambda), clouds (SageMaker, MSFT Foundry, OCI), integrators (Infosys, TCS, HCLTech) and AI natives.
insights.speaker: Chris Alexiuk
insights.so_what: Wide day-one support indicates neoclouds and clouds will serve NVIDIA's open models, reinforcing GPU demand.
insights.locator: Partner ecosystem
